climatology.step_1: for each day-of-year d, pool SST from DOY in [d-5, d+5] (11-day window, wrap-around) across the 30 baseline years; mu(d) = mean, theta90(d) = 90th percentile
climatology.step_2: smooth BOTH mu(d) and theta90(d) with a 31-day centred day-of-year rolling mean (wrap-around)
climatology.leap_day: DOY 366 kept; stabilised by the smoothing window
climatology.ice_masking: SST set NaN where the OISST ice fraction exceeds 0.15, applied identically when building the baseline and when detecting daily exceedance

detection.exceedance: x = max(0, SST - theta90); exceedance day iff x > 0
detection.step_1: keep runs of >= 5 CONSECUTIVE exceedance days
detection.step_2: then merge two kept events separated by a gap of <= 2 days; absorbed gap days become part of the event
detection.note: the >= 5 test applies to consecutive exceedance BEFORE any bridging. This is the letter of Hobday et al. (2016) and what heatwaveR / Oliver's marineHeatWaves implement. The legacy 'bridged_run' mode, which let events confirm on as few as 2 consecutive days, was corrected 2026-07-20 and no shipped result uses it.
detection.A: 1 on every day of a confirmed (possibly merged) event, counted from the event's physical start

intensity_reference.I: I = SST - mu, the SIGNED anomaly above the seasonal climatological mean (heatwaveR 'relSeas'), NOT clamped at 0 and NOT referenced to theta90
intensity_reference.note: Hobday et al. (2016) Table 2 defines i_max / i_mean / i_cum relative to the seasonal mean. The clamp is omitted so i_mean, i_cum and the onset start-edge term match the reference implementation exactly.

no_input_day_rule: Engine rule for a day with no input, as it stands in code at d306292 (update_states.py), stated in words: run_state_engine pre-allocates its per-cell exceedance array over EVERY calendar day of the requested range and writes only the days present in the input, so a day with no input keeps x = 0 and is scored as a day on which no cell exceeded its threshold. Because the >=5-consecutive test is applied BEFORE gaps of <=2 days are bridged, such a day inside a run splits it; if both halves are shorter than 5 days the whole event is discarded, and if it falls inside a <=2-day gap it is absorbed as a bridged gap day (A = 1 with I never written: the area_frac > 0, Ibar = 0 signature). D, C and O then reset for the rest of that event. The engine still behaves this way; what changed is what the PRODUCT discloses. Since a672583 every daily row carries n_days_input (1 if that day's input was read, else 0) and n_cells_valid, and a row with n_days_input = 0 is written NaN in every value column (area_frac, Ibar, Dbar, Cbar, Obar) instead of zero. The monthly product averages over input days only and carries n_days (days aggregated), n_days_input and days_in_month (calendar length). In THIS vintage no row has n_days_input = 0: all eight missing days were obtained as real observations, so the NaN rule is in force but is not triggered. Event-level effects of a future no-input day (a run split by a zero-filled day) are therefore DISCLOSED by n_days_input, not repaired; a vintage with any n_days_input = 0 row should be read with that in mind.

columns.daily: date, area_frac, Ibar, Dbar, Cbar, Obar, n_days_input, n_cells_valid
columns.monthly: date, area_frac, Ibar, Dbar, Cbar, Obar, n_days, n_days_input, days_in_month
columns.n_days_input: daily: 1 if that day's OISST input was read, else 0. monthly: days with input in the month
columns.n_cells_valid: daily: mask cells with a usable observation (not ice-masked, finite SST and theta90). Deliberately NOT n_valid* (gate check 9 prefix)
columns.days_in_month: monthly: calendar length of the month; every month is complete through 2026-08 (no partial terminal month)
columns.monthly_rule: calendar-month mean of the daily series over input days only (every day has input in this vintage, so identical to the plain calendar mean)
columns.names_settled_by: admin ...-18 (final; every earlier naming message void)

caveats.beaufort_zero_valid_cell_days: 4,831 Beaufort days have input present (n_days_input = 1) but n_cells_valid = 0: every mask cell is ice-masked, so no open water exists in which a heatwave could be measured, and every value is 0. Consistent with the rule (ice masking applied identically in baseline and detection), but a reader should know these zeros mean 'no measurable ocean', not 'measured and found quiet'. No other zone has such a day. (lofra-mini's finding; reproduced here.) Count updated for #3: 4,831 (4,808 through 2026-07-01 + 23 in July/August).
caveats.obar_signed: Obar is signed and unclamped: 4 negative daily values (chukchi 2, beaufort 2) + 1 negative monthly (beaufort); most negative daily -0.0248. Unchanged from #1/#2.
caveats.terminal_month: None: the series ends on the last day of August, so the last monthly row is a complete month. The July-excluded derivative is retired (admin ...-20261001-02).

change_vs_vintage_2.mechanism: RIGHT-CENSORING at #2's series end, not a correction. In #2, exceedance runs that began in the last days of June were cut off at 2026-07-01 before reaching 5 consecutive days, so they could not be confirmed. With July data they reach 5 days and are confirmed backwards: area_frac rises and the conditional means move on 2026-06-28..07-01 (nbs, and ebs which contains it), and Obar moves on start days back to 2026-06-13 because events running into July now peak later. Verified per cell: x through 07-01 identical in all zones; every changed A cell-day went 0->1 on a cell continuously active to 07-01.
change_vs_vintage_2.monthly_2026_07: every zone: was a 1-day month (n_days 1 of 31), now complete (31 of 31); values change accordingly
